meta.note: Ubiquitous-language ontology for this repo's domain: the vocabulary the code embodies, and the explicit typed relations between terms (is-a, part-of, relates, persists, references, describes, determines). Deliberately separate from concept_store/concepts.json -- that store is architecture PER MODULE (one summary per file) and answers 'what does this module promise'. This file is vocabulary PER DOMAIN TERM and answers 'what is this thing, and what is it to the others' -- a term here can span several modules (AgentState alone is written and read by a dozen node modules), and a module can define several terms, so it does not fit concept_store's per-file shape. Ground truth is still the code; this is a durable, human-readable map of the graph rather than N separate summaries. Modelled on task-framework/ontology/task-domain.json.

bounded_contexts.ACME Protocol Flow: RFC 8555 vocabulary: accounts, orders, authorizations, challenges, finalization. The wire-level exchange with the certificate authority, independent of how the agent decides to trigger it.
bounded_contexts.Agent Orchestration: The LangGraph machinery that drives ACME Protocol Flow and SPIFFE Attestation Flow to completion: shared state, node callables, routers, and the two compiled graphs (renewal, revocation).
bounded_contexts.SPIFFE Attestation Flow: The alternate, non-ACME issuance path: workload identity via SPIRE Agent's Workload API. Shares Agent Orchestration's state/graph shape but has almost no vocabulary in common with ACME Protocol Flow -- SVIDs and trust domains, not orders and challenges.
bounded_contexts.Certificate Lifecycle Management: What happens to a certificate once key material exists: on-disk storage layout, expiry scanning, renewal planning/prioritisation, and revocation -- the concerns that exist regardless of which flow produced the certificate.
bounded_contexts.Configuration: Settings resolution: which issuance mode is active, which CA provider and directory URL apply, and how operator input (env vars, CLI overrides, MCP call-scoped overrides) is validated and merged.
bounded_contexts.Compliance and Regulation: The project's conformance surface: which RFCs it implements and to which clauses, where it deliberately chooses strictness, and what is out of scope. Cuts across ACME Protocol Flow and Certificate Lifecycle Management -- the spec obligations those contexts must meet, named separately from the code that meets them. doc/RFC_COMPLIANCE.md is the per-clause map; the section numbers cited throughout the other terms and in concept_store resolve against the RFCs collected here.

AgentState.definition: The single TypedDict shared by both the renewal graph and the revocation graph. Every node reads and returns a partial slice of it; LangGraph merges partial returns into the running state. Carries ACME-flow fields (current_order, acme_account_url), SPIFFE-flow fields, and revocation fields side by side, though a given compiled graph only touches one subset. Never carries raw private key material -- only paths to it on disk.

AcmeOrder.definition: One in-flight ACME order, potentially spanning multiple domains (SAN certificate). Its list fields (auth_urls, challenge_urls, challenge_tokens, key_authorizations, auth_domains, dns_txt_values) are parallel arrays, one entry per identifier/authorization, always kept the same length. Held inside AgentState as current_order, not a standalone table.

CertRecord.definition: One domain's scan result: paths to its cert/key on disk (if any), computed expiry and days-until-expiry, whether it needs renewal, and the CA that issued it (advisory only, never authoritative -- see CaMismatchDetection). Produced by CertificateScannerNode, consumed by RenewalPlannerNode.

Challenge.definition: RFC 8555 proof-of-control step for one authorization: HTTP-01 (serve a token at a well-known URL) or DNS-01 (publish a TXT record), chosen once per run via HTTP_CHALLENGE_MODE and never mixed mid-order. Represented in AcmeOrder as parallel entries in challenge_urls/challenge_tokens/key_authorizations, not as its own object.

ChallengeVerifierNode.definition: The node that responds to a Challenge and polls until the CA marks its authorization valid. Checks authorization status before responding, since the CA may already consider an authorization valid from a prior order (RFC 8555 §7.5 reuse) and re-responding to an already-valid challenge is a protocol error.

OrderFinalizerNode.definition: Submits the CSR to an order's finalize URL and polls until the CA hands back a certificate URL, per RFC 8555 §7.4. Transitions AcmeOrder.status toward 'valid' on success or 'invalid' on failure; does not itself download the certificate.

CertDownloaderNode.definition: POST-as-GETs the certificate URL produced by OrderFinalizerNode and stores the returned full PEM chain onto AcmeOrder. Re-downloading is replay-safe per RFC 8555 §7.4.2 -- the certificate URL is stable and idempotent.

NodeCallable.definition: The structural (Protocol, not inheritance) contract every graph node satisfies: callable with an AgentState, returns a dict of partial state updates. The thing that lets NODE_REGISTRY instantiate any registered class uniformly regardless of what ACME/SPIFFE/revocation step it implements.

NodeRegistry.definition: The lookup that turns a node name into a fresh NodeCallable instance for graph wiring. Enforces that every registered value is a class, never a pre-built instance or bare function, so each compiled graph gets its own node state.

RenewalPlannerNode.definition: Decides pending_renewals' order from the scanned CertRecords, either via an LLM (advisory prioritisation only, validated against managed_domains afterward) or a deterministic fallback (no-cert domains first, then soonest-to-expire) when LLM_DISABLED is set. The deterministic path is what actually gates a real renewal decision; the LLM path can only reorder or drop within it, never invent a domain to act on.

ErrorHandlerNode.definition: Classifies an ACME error as fatal (forces abort regardless of retry budget) or retryable (exponential backoff, capped, until max_retries exhausted), writing the decision into AgentState.error_action for ErrorActionRouter to read verbatim -- never re-derived from error_analysis prose.

RetrySchedulerNode.definition: Sleeps until AgentState.retry_not_before elapses, then clears it. Exists to decouple the retry decision (ErrorHandlerNode) from actually enforcing the wait, so a node can be tested/graded on the decision without waiting in real time.

PickNextDomainNode.definition: Pops the next domain off pending_renewals and resets per-domain transient AgentState fields (current_order, current_nonce, retry_count) so each domain's ACME flow starts from a clean slate rather than inheriting the previous domain's in-flight order.

PickNextRevocationDomainNode.definition: The revocation-graph analogue of PickNextDomainNode: pops revocation_targets, sets current_revocation_domain, and resets the per-domain retry budget -- retries are scoped to one domain's revocation attempt, not the whole run.

RevocationLoopRouter.definition: Routes after cert_revoker to one of retry (same domain, via retry_scheduler), next_domain, or all_done. A single domain's revocation failure -- fatal, or transient after exhausting its retry budget -- never halts the run; it is logged into failed_revocations and the loop advances.

SpiffeAttestorNode.definition: SPIFFE mode's analogue of the ACME account/order/challenge/csr/finalizer chain in one node: fetches an SVID for the current SPIFFE ID from the SPIRE Agent's Workload API over a local Unix socket, writes the private key to disk itself (mirroring CsrGeneratorNode's role), and populates current_order.full_chain_pem so the existing storage_manager node can be reused unchanged. A permission-denied response for an unregistered workload is expected non-fatal behaviour, treated the same as any other flow's recoverable error.

SVID.definition: SPIFFE Verifiable Identity Document: the cert + key pair the Workload API hands back for a given SPIFFE ID. The SPIFFE-flow equivalent of an ACME-issued certificate + AcmeOrder.certificate_url, but obtained via local attestation rather than a challenge/response protocol.

AcmeConfig.definition: The pydantic settings class active when CERT_ISSUANCE_MODE=acme: CA_PROVIDER, ACME_DIRECTORY_URL resolution, MANAGED_DOMAINS, EAB credentials. Its fields do not exist at all on the settings object when SpiffeConfig is active instead -- accessing them raises AttributeError, there is no silent default.

SpiffeConfig.definition: The pydantic settings class active when CERT_ISSUANCE_MODE=spiffe: SPIRE_AGENT_SOCKET_PATH, SPIFFE_TRUST_DOMAIN, MANAGED_SPIFFE_IDS. Mutually exclusive with AcmeConfig by construction, never both live in one process.

CertIssuanceMode.definition: The CERT_ISSUANCE_MODE value ('acme' or 'spiffe') that make_settings() dispatches on to construct exactly one of AcmeConfig/SpiffeConfig, and that build_graph() dispatches on to wire exactly one of the ACME or SPIFFE node sets into the compiled StateGraph. The single switch that determines which bounded context (ACME Protocol Flow vs SPIFFE Attestation Flow) is live for a process.

AcmeAccountKey.definition: The ACME account's private key. Deliberately never travels through AgentState (would leak into LangSmith traces) -- only its filesystem path (account_key_path) is kept in state, and any node needing the key loads it fresh from disk.

DomainPrivateKey.definition: The per-domain private key generated alongside a CSR (ACME flow) or handed back by the Workload API (SPIFFE flow). Written straight to disk at mode 0o600 by the node that creates it; its content never appears in AgentState, matching AcmeAccountKey's treatment.

AtomicWrite.definition: A supporting term: kept for the DomainPrivateKey / CertRecord edges below rather than for its own sake -- it is a write mechanism, not a first-class domain noun, so do not read it as one or try to promote it. The temp-file -> fsync -> os.replace() sequence every write into the certificate store passes through (atomic_write_text / atomic_write_bytes, reached via storage.filesystem._write). The temp file is created in the target's own directory so the rename is atomic within one filesystem; a crash mid-write leaves the previous file fully intact and a half-written PEM is never visible to a reader. This is the code behind CLAUDE.md's 'write nothing halfway' principle. The guarantee is per-file, not per-certificate: write_cert_files() writes cert.pem, chain.pem, fullchain.pem, privkey.pem and metadata.json through five separate atomic writes, so a crash between them can leave a new cert.pem beside an old privkey.pem. privkey.pem is chmod'd 0o600 immediately after its atomic write, so it briefly exists at the mkstemp default mode.

Rfc8555.definition: RFC 8555 (Automatic Certificate Management Environment) -- the wire protocol the whole ACME Protocol Flow context implements: directory and nonce, newAccount (with EAB where a CA requires it), newOrder, authorizations, challenges (HTTP-01 §8.3, DNS-01 §8.4), finalize and download (§7.4), revokeCert (§7.6). CLAUDE.md's 'follow the spec, and where the spec is strict, be strict' is about this document. doc/RFC_COMPLIANCE.md is the per-clause conformance map; where a term's definition cites a section number (e.g. AcmeOrder's §7.5 reuse, CertDownloaderNode's §7.4.2) it is a section of this RFC.

Rfc5280.definition: RFC 5280 (X.509 PKI Certificate and CRL Profile) -- referenced here for two distinct things: (1) the CRL reason codes 0-10 (§5.3.1) carried by RevocationReasonCode and validated in acme/client.py:revoke_certificate; (2) the issuer Distinguished Name and Authority Information Access extension (§4.1.2.4, §4.2.2.1) parsed when advisorily detecting which CA issued an on-disk cert (the CaMismatchDetection behaviour noted on CertRecord). Not the certificate-issuance profile in general -- only these two touch points.

Revocation.definition: Permanently invalidating an already-issued certificate before its natural expiry, via a dedicated StateGraph (agent/revocation_graph.py) separate from the renewal graph. One POST to the CA's revokeCert endpoint per RFC 8555 §7.6, carrying the base64url DER certificate and an optional RevocationReasonCode. Irreversible and best-effort: a single domain's failure is logged into failed_revocations and the loop advances (see RevocationLoopRouter), never halting the run. Triggered only on demand (CLI --revoke-cert), never automatically.

RevocationReasonCode.definition: The RFC 5280 §5.3.1 CRL reason code (integer 0-10) attached to a Revocation: in practice 0=unspecified, 1=keyCompromise, 4=superseded, 5=cessationOfOperation. Validated to the 0-10 range in acme/client.py:revoke_certificate; omitted from the revokeCert payload entirely when 0, per RFC 8555 §7.6 which makes the field optional. Comes from a deterministic CLI argument (--reason), never from the LLM -- the revoke-cert skill maps an operator's plain-English cause to a code as advisory input only, the code that acts is the validated integer. reporter.py maps it back to a name for the summary.

AcmeEab.definition: External Account Binding (EAB) -- the HMAC-signed outer JWS that ties a new ACME account to a pre-existing CA account, required by DigiCert, ZeroSSL and Sectigo. Specified in RFC 8555 section 7.3.4 (EAB has no standalone RFC; the draft-ietf-acme-external-account-binding work was folded into RFC 8555 before publication -- RFC 8739 is an unrelated document, STAR certificates). Built by acme/jws.py:create_eab_jws (protected header {alg:HS256, kid:<eab_kid>, url:<newAccount>}, payload = the account public JWK, signature = HMAC-SHA256 over the decoded EAB key -- section 7.3.4 mandates a MAC-based alg but no specific one, HS256 is the project's choice); the key must be >= 16 bytes, an implementation minimum enforced by acme/jws.py:validate_eab_hmac_key (section 7.3.4 sets no key-length rule). Partial EAB config (only one of ACME_EAB_KEY_ID / ACME_EAB_HMAC_KEY set) is rejected before any network call by config.py:AcmeConfig.validate_eab_credentials, and again at newAccount time by acme/client.py:EabAcmeClient.

Rfc7638.definition: RFC 7638 (JSON Web Key Thumbprint) -- the canonical-JSON SHA-256 hash of a public JWK. acme/jws.py:compute_jwk_thumbprint builds the RFC 7638 section 3.2 canonical form for RSA ({e, kty, n} in lexical order, no whitespace) and base64url-encodes the digest; acme/jws.py:compute_key_authorization concatenates token + '.' + thumbprint to form the HTTP-01 and DNS-01 key-authorization that proves control of an identifier. josepy omits 'kty' from its partial JSON, so the code re-adds it explicitly to match what ACME servers expect.

RfcComplianceMap.definition: A supporting term for the doc, not a code noun: doc/RFC_COMPLIANCE.md, the per-clause table mapping every implemented protocol operation to its RFC section (RFC 8555 directory/nonce/account/order/authz/challenge/finalize/revoke, RFC 8555 section 7.3.4 EAB, RFC 7638 thumbprint, RFC 5280 reason codes), together with the explicit strictness choices it records (one nonce consumed per _post_signed, badNonce retried at most _NONCE_RETRIES = 3 times from the error's Replay-Nonce header, parallel domain processing permanently prohibited because a shared nonce cannot be split) and the intentionally-out-of-scope list. It is the human-readable index behind the section numbers cited throughout this ontology and in concept_store.

relations.subject: AcmeOrder
relations.note: Held as AgentState.current_order; no standalone table or id of its own outside the state slice that carries it.

relations.subject: Challenge
relations.note: Represented as parallel list entries (challenge_urls/challenge_tokens/key_authorizations), not a separate object -- the parallel-array invariant across those lists is how a Challenge stays addressable at all.

relations.subject: CertRecord
relations.note: Held as AgentState.cert_records, one per managed domain, produced by scanning and consumed by RenewalPlannerNode.

relations.subject: NodeRegistry
relations.note: Not persistence in the storage sense -- 'persists' here means NodeRegistry is the sole place instances of any NodeCallable are constructed from, matching TaskStore's role for Task in the reference ontology.

relations.subject: CertIssuanceMode
relations.note: make_settings() constructs AcmeConfig only when CERT_ISSUANCE_MODE=='acme'; the SpiffeConfig fields do not exist on the resulting settings object at all.

relations.subject: CertIssuanceMode
relations.note: Symmetric to the AcmeConfig relation above -- exactly one of the two is ever live, never both.

relations.subject: AgentState
relations.note: AgentState carries both ACME-flow and SPIFFE-flow fields simultaneously even though CertIssuanceMode means only one config/flow is active per process -- an intentional shared shape (agent-state-typed-schema in concept_store), not drift.

relations.subject: AgentState
relations.note: Same shared-shape relationship as the AcmeConfig entry above, for the SPIFFE side.

relations.subject: SpiffeAttestorNode
relations.note: Functional analogues across bounded contexts: both are the step that turns an in-flight request into usable cert+key material, one via ACME finalize+download, the other via a single Workload API fetch.

relations.subject: SVID
relations.note: SVID is what SpiffeAttestorNode writes into current_order.full_chain_pem so storage_manager can be reused unchanged -- the SPIFFE flow deliberately borrows AcmeOrder's field as its handoff point rather than defining a parallel one.

relations.subject: AcmeAccountKey
relations.note: Only account_key_path is referenced from state; the key itself is loaded fresh from disk by whichever node needs it, never stored inline -- same treatment DomainPrivateKey gets.

relations.subject: DomainPrivateKey
relations.note: Same non-storage relationship as AcmeAccountKey -- state carries a path or nothing, never key material.

relations.subject: PickNextRevocationDomainNode
relations.note: Not a class inheritance relationship (they are separate classes in separate modules) but the same role in the two graphs: pop the next unit of work, reset per-unit transient state, scope the retry budget to that one unit.

relations.subject: RevocationLoopRouter
relations.note: Deliberately does NOT reuse ErrorHandlerNode's fatal/retryable classification -- revocation-retry-error-classification in concept_store notes the two use inverse defaults (renewal treats unknown errors as retryable; revocation treats them as fatal) because an unrecognised revocation error more likely means a new policy rejection than a new transient failure.

relations.subject: ErrorHandlerNode
relations.note: ErrorHandlerNode decides retry vs abort and sets retry_not_before; RetrySchedulerNode is the only node that actually waits on it, then clears it -- the decision and the enforcement are deliberately separate nodes.

relations.subject: CertDownloaderNode
relations.note: CertDownloaderNode reads AcmeOrder.certificate_url, which only OrderFinalizerNode ever sets -- a one-directional dependency expressed only through shared AgentState fields, not a function call between the two.

relations.subject: CertRecord
relations.note: A CertRecord holds the on-disk cert/key paths that write_cert_files produced; AtomicWrite is why a CertRecord scanned right after a crashed renewal still points at the intact previous cert rather than a truncated file.

relations.subject: DomainPrivateKey
relations.note: privkey.pem is written via atomic_write_text and then chmod'd 0o600 by write_cert_files -- two steps, so the key exists briefly at the mkstemp default mode between the atomic rename and the chmod. AtomicWrite protects the file's contents; it does not make the create+chmod a single operation.

relations.subject: AcmeOrder
relations.note: AcmeOrder's whole lifecycle -- newOrder, the parallel authorization/challenge arrays, finalize, download -- is RFC 8555 §7.4 vocabulary; the section numbers cited in AcmeOrder's and CertDownloaderNode's definitions are sections of this RFC.

relations.subject: Challenge
relations.note: HTTP-01 is RFC 8555 §8.3, DNS-01 is §8.4; the key-authorization construction and the already-valid-authorization reuse rule (§7.5) that ChallengeVerifierNode guards against both come from this RFC.

relations.subject: Revocation
relations.note: The revokeCert request shape -- POST-as-GET-style signed POST of the base64url DER cert to the directory's revokeCert URL, optional reason field -- is RFC 8555 §7.6.

relations.subject: Revocation
relations.note: The reason field carried by a Revocation is an RFC 5280 §5.3.1 CRL reason code, surfaced here as RevocationReasonCode.

relations.subject: RevocationReasonCode
relations.note: Not a standalone entity -- it is the optional integer field on a single Revocation request, held in AgentState as revocation_reason and validated to 0-10 by acme/client.py:revoke_certificate.

relations.subject: Revocation
relations.note: RevocationLoopRouter is the per-domain loop that drives one Revocation attempt at a time, deciding retry / next_domain / all_done after cert_revoker -- the orchestration around the protocol act, in the same shape PickNextDomainNode + the renewal loop wrap a renewal.

relations.subject: RfcComplianceMap
relations.note: doc/RFC_COMPLIANCE.md's 'RFC 8555 -- ACME Protocol' tables are the per-operation conformance map; every section number cited on Rfc8555 (and on AcmeOrder, Challenge, CertDownloaderNode, Revocation) is indexed there.

relations.subject: RfcComplianceMap
relations.note: The doc's 'RFCs Referenced' table and revocation section record the two RFC 5280 touch points -- reason codes (section 5.3.1) and issuer DN / AIA parsing -- that Rfc5280 scopes.

relations.subject: RfcComplianceMap
relations.note: The doc's 'RFC 8555 section 7.3.4 -- External Account Binding' section maps EAB account creation for DigiCert / ZeroSSL / Sectigo.

relations.subject: RfcComplianceMap
relations.note: The doc lists 'RFC 7638 -- JWK Thumbprint' as the basis of HTTP-01 and DNS-01 key-authorization computation.

relations.subject: AcmeEab
relations.note: EAB is the outer JWS wrapped around RFC 8555's newAccount request; the binding is defined in RFC 8555 section 7.3.4. EabAcmeClient overrides only the newAccount payload, everything else is the plain Rfc8555 flow.

relations.subject: Challenge
relations.note: The key-authorization a Challenge proves (token + '.' + thumbprint) uses the RFC 7638 section 3.2 canonical JWK thumbprint from acme/jws.py:compute_jwk_thumbprint for both HTTP-01 and DNS-01.

relations.subject: AcmeConfig
relations.note: AcmeConfig carries ACME_EAB_KEY_ID / ACME_EAB_HMAC_KEY and validate_eab_credentials rejects a partial pair before any network call -- the config-side half of the EAB obligation AcmeEab names.
